bugs.name: Malassezia furfur
bugs.symptoms: Hypo/hyperpigmented trunk macules; spaghetti-and-meatballs on KOH
bugs.treatment: Selenium sulfide shampoo or topical antifungals

bugs.name: Trichophyton rubrum
bugs.symptoms: Annular scaly plaque with central clearing; branching hyphae on KOH
bugs.treatment: Topical antifungals; oral terbinafine for widespread disease

bugs.name: Corynebacterium minutissimum
bugs.symptoms: Brown intertriginous patches; coral-red fluorescence on Wood's lamp

bugs.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bugs.symptoms: Scalded tender skin with flaccid bullae, mucosa SPARED, positive Nikolsky
bugs.treatment: IV nafcillin or oxacillin (vancomycin if MRSA)

bugs.name: Neisseria meningitidis
bugs.geography: Worldwide; outbreaks in crowded living (dorms, military)
bugs.symptoms: Fever, neck stiffness, altered mentation, petechial/purpuric rash

bugs.name: Group A Streptococcus
bugs.symptoms: Pain out of proportion, crepitus, rapidly spreading systemic toxicity
bugs.treatment: Immediate surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum antibiotics

bugs.name: Rickettsia rickettsii
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache, petechial rash starting at wrists/ankles spreading centrally

bugs.name: Varicella-zoster virus
bugs.symptoms: Unilateral V1 vesicular rash; Hutchinson sign (vesicles on nose tip)
bugs.treatment: Oral acyclovir/valacyclovir within 72 h plus urgent ophthalmology consult

bugs.name: Measles virus (Rubeola)
bugs.symptoms: Cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots, cephalocaudal rash
bugs.treatment: Supportive care plus vitamin A; MMR vaccine for prevention

bugs.name: Herpes simplex virus
bugs.symptoms: Targetoid lesions with dusky center on palms and soles

bugs.name: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1)
bugs.symptoms: CD4 decline, opportunistic infections, severe seborrheic dermatitis
bugs.treatment: Two NRTIs plus an integrase inhibitor (dolutegravir or bictegravir)

drugs.name: Tenofovir (TDF/TAF)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone); also hepatitis B
drugs.mechanism: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor causing DNA chain termination
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity (Fanconi syndrome) and decreased bone density; TAF milder

drugs.name: Emtricitabine (FTC)
drugs.mechanism: Cytidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Lamivudine (3TC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone); also hepatitis B
drugs.mechanism: Cytidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Abacavir (ABC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone partner with lamivudine)
drugs.mechanism: Guanosine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA
drugs.adverseEffects: Fatal hypersensitivity in HLA-B*5701 carriers; never rechallenge

drugs.name: Zidovudine (AZT)
drugs.disease: HIV vertical-transmission prevention in pregnancy and neonates
drugs.mechanism: Thymidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Dolutegravir (DTG)
drugs.mechanism: Second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Weight gain; high resistance barrier and well tolerated

drugs.name: Bictegravir (BIC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (first-line third agent, fixed-dose Biktarvy)
drugs.mechanism: Second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Weight gain; well tolerated, high resistance barrier

drugs.name: Raltegravir (RAL)
drugs.mechanism: First-generation INSTI metabolized by UGT1A1, not CYP
drugs.adverseEffects: Lower resistance barrier; no CYP-based drug interactions

drugs.name: Cabotegravir (CAB)
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting injectable integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Injection-site reactions; gluteal IM every 4-8 weeks

drugs.name: Efavirenz
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor

drugs.name: Rilpivirine
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor
drugs.adverseEffects: Needs acid stomach for absorption; virologic failure at high VL

drugs.name: Nevirapine
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection; presumptive therapy in high-risk neonates
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor

drugs.name: Atazanavir
drugs.mechanism: Protease inhibitor blocking gag/gag-pol polyprotein cleavage

drugs.name: Darunavir
drugs.mechanism: Protease inhibitor blocking gag/gag-pol polyprotein cleavage
drugs.adverseEffects: Sulfa-moiety rash; avoid in sulfa allergy; hepatotoxicity

drugs.name: Ritonavir / Cobicistat
drugs.disease: Pharmacokinetic boosting of HIV protease inhibitors
drugs.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises partner PI levels

drugs.name: Maraviroc
drugs.mechanism: CCR5 antagonist blocking gp120 co-receptor engagement
drugs.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity; requires tropism testing before use

drugs.name: Enfuvirtide
drugs.mechanism: gp41 fusion inhibitor; 36-amino-acid synthetic peptide

drugs.name: Lenacapavir
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced patients
drugs.mechanism: Capsid inhibitor disrupting uncoating, nuclear import, assembly

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.mechanism: Antimalarial immunomodulator reducing autoimmune inflammation

drugs.name: Dapsone
drugs.mechanism: Sulfone with anti-inflammatory/antimicrobial activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Hemolysis, especially in G6PD deficiency; methemoglobinemia

drugs.name: Vismodegib
drugs.disease: Locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma
drugs.mechanism: Smoothened inhibitor blocking Hedgehog pathway signaling

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil (topical)
drugs.disease: Actinic keratosis field treatment; superficial BCC and SCC in situ
drugs.mechanism: Topical antimetabolite chemotherapy killing dysplastic keratinocytes
drugs.adverseEffects: Local erythema, erosion, inflammation during treatment

drugs.name: Propranolol
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective beta-blocker promoting hemangioma involution

drugs.name: Intramuscular epinephrine
drugs.disease: Anaphylaxis with urticaria and airway compromise
drugs.mechanism: Alpha/beta agonist reversing vasodilation and bronchospasm

drugs.name: Icatibant
drugs.mechanism: Bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist
drugs.adverseEffects: Injection-site reactions; ineffective for histaminergic angioedema

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.disease: Toxic shock syndrome and necrotizing soft-tissue infection
drugs.mechanism: Ribosomal inhibitor that suppresses bacterial exotoxin production

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.mechanism: Tetracycline antibiotic; 30S ribosomal protein-synthesis inhibitor
drugs.adverseEffects: Tooth discoloration in children; benefit outweighs risk in RMSF

drugs.name: Nifedipine
drugs.mechanism: Calcium channel blocker causing peripheral vasodilation

drugs.name: Alteplase (thrombolytics)
drugs.mechanism: Tissue plasminogen activator lysing microvascular thrombi

drugs.name: Dantrolene
drugs.disease: Malignant hyperthermia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Ryanodine receptor blocker stopping skeletal muscle Ca release

drugs.name: Benzodiazepines (lorazepam/diazepam)
drugs.disease: Shivering suppression during heat stroke cooling
drugs.mechanism: GABA-A potentiation suppressing the shivering reflex

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.disease: Refractory hypotension in heat stroke or hypothermia
drugs.mechanism: Beta-agonist augmenting cardiac contractility without vasoconstriction

correlates.name: Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Reconstituted immunity on ART suddenly attacks subclinical opportunistic infections
correlates.treatment: Continue ART; treat the underlying infection; steroids if severe

correlates.name: NRTI Lactic Acidosis with Hepatic Steatosis
correlates.pathophysiology: NRTI inhibition of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma impairs oxidative phosphorylation
correlates.treatment: Discontinue NRTI immediately; supportive care for lactate clearance

correlates.name: Abacavir Hypersensitivity Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Abacavir binds HLA-B*5701, creating a neo-self-antigen recognized by cytotoxic T cells
correlates.treatment: Stop abacavir permanently; never rechallenge (can be fatal)

correlates.name: Nevirapine Hepatotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: Hypersensitivity-mediated hepatocellular injury, worse with higher CD4 counts
correlates.treatment: Stop nevirapine immediately and permanently; supportive care

correlates.name: Protease Inhibitor Lipodystrophy
correlates.pathophysiology: PIs impair GLUT4 glucose uptake and adipocyte differentiation via SREBP interference
correlates.treatment: Switch to non-PI regimen; CYP-safe statins; metformin; diet and exercise

correlates.name: Psoriasis
correlates.pathophysiology: T-cell (Th1/Th17) driven keratinocyte hyperproliferation with parakeratosis
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids/vitamin D, phototherapy, methotrexate, biologics

correlates.name: Stasis Dermatitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic venous hypertension causes capillary leak and hemosiderin deposition
correlates.treatment: Compression therapy (cornerstone), leg elevation, topical steroids

correlates.name: Pityriasis Rosea
correlates.pathophysiology: Self-limited eruption, possibly HHV-6/7 triggered; herald patch then Christmas-tree rash
correlates.treatment: Symptomatic care; antihistamines and reassurance

correlates.name: Lichen Planus
correlates.pathophysiology: T-cell-mediated interface dermatitis; strong hepatitis C association
correlates.treatment: Topical/intralesional steroids; phototherapy; treat underlying HCV

correlates.name: Mycosis Fungoides
correlates.pathophysiology: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma progressing through patch, plaque, and tumor stages
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids and phototherapy early; systemic therapy for advanced disease

correlates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
correlates.pathophysiology: Loss of self-tolerance with antinuclear autoantibodies and immune-complex deposition
correlates.treatment: Photoprotection, hydroxychloroquine, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants

correlates.name: Dermatomyositis
correlates.pathophysiology: Humoral autoimmune attack on perimysial capillaries causing muscle ischemia
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids, methotrexate/azathioprine; screen for occult malignancy

correlates.name: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)
correlates.pathophysiology: Fibroblast overproduction of collagen sclerosing skin and internal organs
correlates.treatment: Immunosuppressants; ACE inhibitors for scleroderma renal crisis

correlates.name: Sarcoidosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Th1-driven non-caseating granulomatous inflammation of unknown cause
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids first-line; methotrexate or hydroxychloroquine

correlates.name: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Somatic GNAQ mutation causing V1 port wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomas
correlates.treatment: Anticonvulsants, pulsed-dye laser, IOP control for glaucoma

correlates.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Cumulative UV damage and PTCH1 loss driving Hedgehog pathway activation
correlates.treatment: Excision or Mohs surgery; vismodegib for advanced disease

correlates.name: Melanoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced malignant transformation of melanocytes, often BRAF V600E mutant
correlates.treatment: Wide local excision; immunotherapy and BRAF/MEK inhibitors for advanced disease

correlates.name: Actinic Keratosis
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced p53-driven keratinocyte dysplasia; premalignant precursor to SCC
correlates.treatment: Cryotherapy, topical 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod, photodynamic therapy

correlates.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV or HPV-driven malignant keratinocytes invading through the basement membrane
correlates.treatment: Excision (Mohs for high-risk sites); cemiplimab for advanced disease

correlates.name: Hereditary Angioedema
correlates.pathophysiology: C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency causes uncontrolled bradykinin-mediated edema
correlates.treatment: Icatibant, ecallantide, C1-INH concentrate, or FFP; early intubation

correlates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
correlates.pathophysiology: Drug-specific CD8 T-cell-mediated keratinocyte apoptosis with epidermal detachment
correlates.treatment: Stop offending drug; burn unit; fluid resuscitation and wound care

correlates.name: Toxic Shock Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Superantigen-driven massive T-cell activation, cytokine storm, and capillary leak
correlates.treatment: Remove source; clindamycin plus vancomycin; fluids and vasopressors

correlates.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein-3 cause intraepidermal flaccid bullae
correlates.treatment: Systemic corticosteroids, rituximab; IVIG/plasmapheresis if severe

correlates.name: DRESS Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Delayed type IV drug hypersensitivity with eosinophilia and visceral organ injury
correlates.treatment: Withdraw offending drug; ICU support; long corticosteroid taper

correlates.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapidly spreading bacterial soft-tissue infection with fascial necrosis from toxins
correlates.treatment: Immediate surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum antibiotics

correlates.name: Kawasaki Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Medium-vessel vasculitis of childhood causing coronary artery aneurysms
correlates.treatment: IVIG plus high-dose aspirin; echocardiogram after diagnosis

correlates.name: Frostbite
correlates.pathophysiology: Tissue freezing forms ice crystals; rewarming triggers microvascular thrombosis
correlates.treatment: Rapid rewarming in 37-39 C water; analgesia, tetanus, thrombolytics if severe

correlates.name: Accidental Hypothermia
correlates.pathophysiology: Core temperature below 35 C impairs metabolism, causing bradyarrhythmias and arrest
correlates.treatment: Staged rewarming (passive to active core/ECMO); not dead until warm and dead

correlates.name: Trench Foot (Immersion Foot)
correlates.pathophysiology: Prolonged wet, non-freezing exposure causes neurovascular injury without freezing
correlates.treatment: Remove wet footwear, dry the feet, loose dressing, delay debridement

correlates.name: Chilblains (Pernio)
correlates.pathophysiology: Intermittent damp non-freezing cold causes inflammatory violaceous nodules
correlates.treatment: Nifedipine plus supportive care; warming and time

correlates.name: Heat Stroke
correlates.pathophysiology: Core temperature above 40 C causes protein denaturation and multi-organ failure
correlates.treatment: Aggressive evaporative cooling, IV fluids, ICU; antipyretics are useless

correlates.name: Heat Exhaustion
correlates.pathophysiology: Heat-related volume and electrolyte depletion with preserved mental status
correlates.treatment: Cool environment, leg elevation, oral or IV fluid/electrolyte replacement

correlates.name: Rhabdomyolysis
correlates.pathophysiology: Skeletal muscle breakdown releases myoglobin, risking tubular obstruction and AKI
correlates.treatment: Aggressive isotonic IV fluids; treat the underlying cause
